deck_zh: 炮火来了，决定必须快。但国家的存亡，不能成为让人闭嘴、让权力留下、让居民无路可走的理由。
deck_en: An attack may leave no time to deliberate. It does not answer whom the state is defending, when emergency power must end, or who gets to ask.
body_zh: 指令写得并不凶狠：苇镇不组织撤离；居民自行离开不受限制；公共交通照常。
这是本系列虚构的目的联合城邦。邻国正在炮击苇镇，步兵随后将渡河而来。指令的理由是，组织撤离会向对方表明本国放弃西滩，还会引起后方恐慌。同一天，首席执政在讲话中说，寸土不让，与苇镇同在，直到最后一人。防卫小组三个人，二比一通过了指令。外事执政投了反对票。
地区政府想调大巴接人，防卫署要求军事通行证。证过了三天才发。其间另组织了一次夜间徒步撤离。敌军第九日进入苇镇，控制五周。此前约六成一居民已经离开。留下的有老人、病人，有不愿走的人，也有在医院与供水站值守的人。交战与占领期间，一百四十名平民死亡。到第十二年，死因与责任的分项仍在调查。
不能把这一个数字全部算到一张指令上。炮击是谁发动的，作战造成了什么，通行证为什么晚发，各有各的事实要查。但有一件不必等调查结束才能看见：在那张文书上，先出现的是向外表明什么，后出现的才是人怎样活下来。次序已经倒了。
## 国家需要人，不等于可以拿人去保国家
国家快没了，还有什么不能暂停？这是紧急时最有力量的一句话。目的联合城邦的首席执政也说过。十一万邻国军队在界河西岸集结，评估认为七十二小时内就可能渡河。此时要他等所有程序从容走完，当然不现实。可从来不及等，走不到此后什么都由我决定。
国家值得保住，是因为它守着人的生活、权利和彼此合作的条件。这个理由来自人，不来自国家对自身的热爱。若为了保存它，反而可以封住人的嘴、堵住人的申诉、要求所有人共同赴死，保护的理由便吃掉了它要保护的东西。失去一块土地、一个首都，甚至一套建制，是沉重的失败；却不能因此宣布，既然它们保不住了，人也不必再继续生活。
苇镇的指令没有禁止离开。但能自己走，不等于想走的人走得了。老人、病人需要车辆，车辆需要通行证。组织撤离，不是强迫每个人搬走；它应当给愿走却走不了的人实际的路。选择留下的人，也没有因此放弃保护与供给。不能拿后方的安静去换他们的安危，更不能把不撤离当成一面向敌人展示的旗。
这篇谈的是国家应受什么限制，不是在介绍现行军事法律。它也不是要求决策者预知一切。那三天里车辆为什么不能通行，必须由掌握许可的人说明；一百四十人的责任必须分项核实。坚持这些，既不减轻攻击者的责任，也不允许本国的那一份躲到攻击者背后。
## 军队只有一套指挥，权力不能只有一道门
反对权力独占，容易被听成凡事都要几个人同时点头，甚至军队也得各听各的。那当然无法作战。问题不在一支军队要不要统一指挥，而在指挥它的人能不能同时独自决定：何时转入战时，何时对居民用兵，何时不再受平时约束，又由谁宣布这些已经结束。

铁谷特区两家军工厂罢工，防卫军一个团进入厂区，在厂门设检查站，待了六周。特区没有请求，地方议事会反对，全国议会也没有被提请确认。下令的一方说，这是保护军事供给设施，不是对内用兵。但走过检查站的是工人，拘人也借着检查站进行。名字不能替行动定性。对居民使用军队，至少需要不由指挥者独占的确认，说明用多少、在哪里、到什么时候。法院依法作出的、须强制执行的裁决，也可以构成这样的确认，用兵以执行裁决为限。确认过了，仍要解释必要性、权限与具体手段。这里立的是功能，不是只有一种机关设计才合格。
这里不能再偷走一步，说既然军队进厂缺了确认，关于罢工的一切处置就都已判完。工会后来进入仲裁，地方政府请求法院审查，被起诉者有法院可去；这些路要分别看。为什么仲裁到第六周才开启，一名工人的骨折怎样造成，也要分别查。反过来，这些后来存在的路，也补不上当初未经确认就进厂的缺口。
同样，部队换防、留在既有基地而不向居民执行任务，不因发生在国内就一概算对内用兵。但若恰在南湾邦公投前一周调来两个营，又没有事先告知当地政府，人们仍有理由问：为什么是现在，防的是什么？时点值得核查，不等于已经证明这是威慑。
平时与战时的指挥安排也要分开。战时可以集中，是因为正在打仗；和平时期不能继续借这份理由集中。两套安排之间如何转换，要有不由一个位置独定、带期限、可追问的决定。否则，只要不宣布战时结束，特殊的统辖方式便能一直留下。
紧急状态的期限也一样。原来的制度要求七日内确认、每次六十日，再延长要由联席会议决定。修宪以后，宣布紧急的执政院可以自行续期，议会要以五分之三才能叫停。后来一百七十六票主张终止，一百四十二票反对，普通多数赞成结束，却没有达到门槛。临时权力最容易在这里变成长久的：不是没人说结束，而是结束需要它自己不愿满足的条件。
审查者与宣布者同属一个多数，不能单凭这一点就说审查是假。要看前者能否获得材料，能否独立作判断，能否让措施真的停下。反过来，机构名称不同也不保证独立。若战争状态不结束，议会自己的任期就延长，它在这一件事上的位置，也需要重看。
最难的反问是，假如议会被炸，凑不齐法定人数呢？替补安排应在事前准备，而不能由宣布紧急的人临时挑一个同意自己的人来确认。常规与替补都无法行动时，临时措施只能限于事前写明的最短期限，不得自行续期。这个要求不保证灾难里程序总能保住；它只是拒绝把程序一时被毁，解释成做过的决定从此不必说明。已有的有效终审裁决，也不因新宣布的临时措施而可以搁置。
六百四十人的拘留便说明了问到与问得动的区别。每次三十日，看上去有期限，但可以连续，续不续由拘留者决定，最长已达一百五十日。监察署可以调卷、要求说明，却不能放人。法院审条款合不合宪章，仍不等于每一个人能请独立位置复核自己的拘留。按卷中给出的配置，欠的恰恰是这条能使人出来的路。若另查出确有可用的个案复核，各人的判断应据事实重核，不能拿一个总标签代替。
## 临时权力，不能等自己愿意离开
战争结束后再处理。军中一个二十岁青年听到的，也是这句话。他没有宗教归属，却因良心不愿持武器，申请替代服务。申请收了，战时暂停审查；拒不应征可能坐牢二至五年。他入伍，服役两年。等恢复审查，委员会告诉他：已经服完，不再审了。

恰恰因为已经服完，才更该回答当初为什么不能审。要问的不是他今后还用不用当兵，而是那两年里，他的拒绝为什么没有去处。申请应当随时能提出，在役也可以，不以有无宗教为条件；待审期间不强迫入伍、不提起相应追诉，驳回可请法院复核。审查核申请是否针对持武器本身、前后是否一贯，不替人终审内心的真伪。替代服务可以有负担，差别须有公开理由，不能设计成报复。只反对某一场战争、某一种任务的申请怎样处理，原论文尚未解决，不能顺手说这已经给每项命令发了个人否决权。
紧急权力还会用更客气的方式留下。战时附加税改叫重建税，监听等到和约签订才停，紧急征用的农田写着战后另议。名称变了，握在手里的东西未必变。和平协议也可能迟迟不来；若所有结束都等那一天，临时就可能没有尽头。
因此要问的不是当局宣布战争何时结束，而是当初迫使防守发生的攻击是否已经解除。在这份虚构记录里，进攻者已被赶回河西，次年春天双方停火，原先防卫的紧迫根据到此用完。议会又过了一年多才终止战时状态，不能倒过来为中间那段时间提供根据。继续驻在对岸，是新的行动，需要另行说明；不能把它藏在原来防卫的授权里。
依战争而成立的权限，到这个终点就失去根据，握着它的人要主动交还，不等反对者证明已经用不着。平时确实需要防线、防务经费或某种公共功能，可以重新作决定：现在为什么要、用到哪里、受谁检查、到什么时候。可以事先安排衔接，不必制造空当；但不能借旧战争续命。普通防务预算并不全是战时临时权力，不能只看军费比例便要求一律撤掉。判断要落在每一项安排的来处与当下根据上。
若敌对时断时续，认不出清楚终点，也不是无限授权的理由。授权要自带期限，延长是新的决定，须重新说明并经独立确认。若原来没有期限，或只写等和约，就要在事前规定的短期内重立为有期限的新安排，否则失效。世界没有替人准备一个漂亮的结束，并不等于权力可以自己决定永远继续。
真正要守住的，始终是人还能往下过的生活。苇镇的土地重要，国家的建制重要，那位青年的两年也重要。保护这些生活的工具，不能要求生活反过来证明工具值得永远留下。
body_en: The directive did not sound brutal: no organized evacuation of Reedtown; residents free to leave on their own; public transport to run as usual.

This is the fictional United City-States of Ends. The neighboring army is shelling Reedtown and will soon cross the river. The written reason for refusing evacuation is that it would signal abandonment of the West Flats and cause panic farther inland. That day the First Executive promises to stand with the town 'to the last person.' The defense subgroup approves the directive two votes to one. The Executive for External Affairs dissents.

The regional government orders buses. The Office of Defense requires military passes, issued three days later. Meanwhile, a separate evacuation on foot takes place at night. Enemy troops enter on the ninth day and hold Reedtown for five weeks. About 61 percent of residents have left. The old, the sick, people unwilling to leave home, and staff keeping the hospital and water station running are among those who remain. One hundred forty civilians die during the fighting and occupation. The division of causes and responsibilities is still being investigated in Year 12.

We cannot charge every death to one directive. Enemy shelling, combat, and delayed passes require separate investigation. But something is already visible in the document: what the country must signal comes before how its people will survive. The order of reasons is wrong.
## Saving the country—for whom?

If the state itself is at stake, what cannot be suspended? Few questions sound more compelling in an emergency. In this case, the assessment is 110,000 troops assembled across the Boundary River, capable of crossing within seventy-two hours. A government may have to act before ordinary deliberation is possible. But no time to wait does not mean unlimited authority thereafter.

A state matters because of the lives, rights, and possibilities of cooperation it protects. Its survival borrows its importance from them. If preserving it authorizes silencing those people, blocking their complaints, or demanding that the entire community die with its institutions, the means has consumed its purpose. Losing territory, a capital, or a political formation can be a devastating defeat. It is not a reason to declare that people's lives must end with it.

Reedtown's residents were not forbidden to leave. Yet permission to walk away is not an evacuation route for a sick person who needs a bus. Organizing evacuation need not mean forcing everyone out. It means making departure possible for those who want it but cannot manage alone. Those who choose to stay do not forfeit protection and supplies. Their safety cannot be exchanged for reassurance elsewhere, or made into a flag displayed to the enemy.

These are proposed limits on state power, not a report of existing military law. Nor do they demand omniscience. They demand explanations: why were the passes delayed? What caused each death? An aggressor's responsibility does not erase a defending administration's decisions. Its decisions do not erase the aggressor's responsibility either.
## One chain of command, more than one source of authority

Checks on military power need not mean rival armies or several officials issuing incompatible battlefield orders. One force needs a coherent command. A different question is whether its commander also gets sole authority to declare war status, use troops against residents, suspend ordinary constraints, and decide when all this is over.

At two Iron Valley arms factories, a strike brought an army regiment to the gates for six weeks. It set up checkpoints and assisted arrests. The local district had not requested deployment, its assembly opposed it, and the national Joint Assembly had not been asked to confirm it. The executive said it was protecting military supply facilities, not deploying against residents. But workers were passing through those checkpoints. A label cannot decide what an operation is doing.

Domestic use of the army requires confirmation not monopolized by its commanders, specifying scope, place, and duration. A lawful court ruling requiring enforcement can supply that confirmation, limited to its enforcement. This is a functional requirement, not a claim that only one institutional design can work. Confirmation is necessary, not a complete justification: authority, necessity, and the means used still require scrutiny. And separate questions stay separate. The union eventually reached arbitration; the district sought court review; prosecuted workers had access to courts. We cannot therefore declare that every avenue of refusal was sealed. Why arbitration took six weeks, and how a worker suffered a broken bone, remain questions. None of those avenues retrospectively supplies the missing deployment confirmation.

Conversely, moving troops between existing bases without deploying them against residents is not automatically domestic military intervention. Yet two battalions moved into South Bay's naval base a week before its secession referendum invite an explanation. Timing deserves examination; it is not already proof of intimidation.

Peacetime and wartime command arrangements must also be distinct. Concentrated wartime authority draws its reason from the war; peace cannot borrow that reason indefinitely. Moving between the arrangements needs a time-limited, challengeable decision not monopolized by one office. Otherwise special command lasts merely because nobody empowered to do so declares it over.

Emergency powers have the same distinction. Originally, the emergency needed confirmation within seven days and renewal by the Joint Assembly every sixty days. After amendment, the Executive Council could renew it itself, while termination required three-fifths of the Assembly. A later vote favored ending it, 176 to 142, but failed the threshold. Temporary authority becomes durable not only when nobody wants it to end, but when ending requires conditions its holders can evade.

Party affiliation alone does not establish that review is fictitious. Reviewers need information, the ability to judge independently, and power to stop a measure. Different institutional names alone prove little either. If continued war status extends legislators' own terms, their independence on that particular question needs another look.

What if the assembly has been bombed and cannot meet? Alternative confirmation arrangements must be prepared beforehand, not improvised by the leader choosing someone willing to approve him. If both ordinary and substitute bodies are disabled, provisional measures are confined to the shortest pre-specified term and cannot renew themselves. This is no promise that procedures will survive every catastrophe. It denies that their temporary destruction wipes out the obligation to answer afterward. New provisional measures do not permit the executive to shelve an already effective final judgment.

The difference between receiving a complaint and changing someone's position is stark in detention. Six hundred forty people are held under a clause allowing thirty-day terms, renewable by the detaining side; the longest detention has reached 150 days. The Inspectorate can inspect files and demand explanations but cannot release anyone. Constitutional review of the clause is not an independent review of each detention. On the arrangements described, that missing release route is the violation. If investigation establishes an effective individual review not recorded here, those cases must be reassessed on their facts.
## Temporary power cannot wait for its own consent to leave

A twenty-year-old from Levee Street hears a familiar promise: after the war. He objects to bearing arms on grounds of conscience, without religious affiliation, and applies for alternative service. His application is received but review is suspended. Refusal to report carries two to five years in prison. He serves for two years. When review resumes, the board answers: service completed; no further review.

Precisely because those years cannot be returned, his application still needs an answer. The question is not whether he must serve next year, but whether he should have been forced to bear arms then. Applications must be available during service as well as before it, without a religious test. Pending review, there must be no compulsory induction or prosecution for the refusal at issue; rejection must be open to court review. Review checks whether the application concerns bearing arms itself and is consistent, not whether an official certifies the person's inner conscience as true. Alternative service can impose burdens, but differences need public reasons and cannot be retaliation. Objection to one war or one kind of mission remains an unresolved question in the paper; this route is not a personal veto over every order.

Emergency power can stay in more courteous forms. A wartime surcharge becomes a reconstruction tax. Surveillance ends when a peace treaty is signed. Requisitioned farmland will be reconsidered 'after the war.' Names change while control remains. Peace treaties may never arrive.

The relevant endpoint is therefore not simply the government's announcement. It is the removal of the attack that made defensive war necessary. In this fictional record, the invading forces have been driven back across the river and hostilities cease the following spring. The original defensive necessity ends there, although formal war status continues for more than another year. Staying on the other bank is a new action needing its own justification, not an extension silently supplied by the original defense.

Powers grounded in that war lose their basis at that endpoint. Their holders must dismantle them, rather than wait for opponents to prove them unnecessary. A peacetime defensive line or public function can be established anew: why now, within what limits, under whose review, and until when? Arrangements can be made in advance so there need be no operational gap. They cannot run on the old war's authority. Ordinary defense expenditure is not all a temporary wartime power; a budget percentage alone cannot tell us what must go. Each arrangement needs its own account of origin and present basis.

Where hostilities recur and no clear endpoint can be identified, authorization still needs an expiry date and independent confirmation. Renewal is a fresh decision. Powers with no term, or only a promise to end at a future peace treaty, must be re-established as time-limited decisions within a pre-specified short period or lapse. An untidy conflict is not an invitation to permanent emergency.

What needs saving is the possibility of people going on with their lives. Reedtown's territory matters; political institutions matter; the young man's two years matter too. The instruments that protect a life cannot require that life to prove why they should ever be relinquished.
